content:
rachel: Quick question for the maintainers: we're getting a couple of bug reports from community users about the Ruby SDK's retry behavior when the auth token rotates. Seems to surface in rails apps with connection pooling. Anyone seen this?

tyler: We had a similar report last month. The SDK retries on 401 but sometimes keeps using the pooled socket which causes silent failures until the next request.

omar: Short-term workaround for apps: set `persistent: false` in the client config or bump the adapter to close connections on refresh. Not ideal.

rachel: Is there appetite for a small patch that calls a public `reset_connection!` after token refresh? That would be a tiny maintenance PR and help users in the wild.

tyler: Yes, please. Keep it minimal: add method on the HTTP client wrapper, call it after refresh, add one unit test asserting it's invoked. Note in the CHANGELOG that it's a compatibility fix for Faraday/net-http-persistent versions.

omar: Also add a short blurb in the sampleapp onboarding Troubleshooting section: "If you see auth-retry hangs, try disabling connection pooling or upgrade net-http-persistent." Helps support.

rachel: I'll open a PR and ping for reviews. Will label `maintenance` and `backport` if needed.

devex-bot: PR created by rachel: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ruby-sdk/pull/291 (private). CI triggered. :rocket:

tyler: Thanks — ping me for review, I can help write the tiny test.

omar: One more thought: let's add a smoke job to devex pipelines that runs the sampleapp auth refresh once on PRs touching `lib/redwood/http_client.rb`. Cheap and catches regressions.

rachel: Done, included in PR. Keeping the smoke job single-scenario and fast.

devex-bot: CI run queued for PR #291.
